correctness.rationale: For a fixed alternating matrix B of rank 2s, the cone border x preserves rank exactly when x lies in im(B), which has q^(2s) elements; otherwise the rank rises by exactly two. Congruence removes borders in im(B), while a border outside im(B) pairs the new coordinate nontrivially with the radical ker(B), adding one nondegenerate alternating plane. Partitioning old specializations by rank yields the stated recurrence with all quantifiers and boundary conventions explicit. The complete-tripartite formula follows by substituting the independently verified rank distribution of the complete-bipartite block. The argument is characteristic-free.

A later published record strengthens the rank reduction to every characteristic and gives complete-bipartite and complete-graph formulas, but no cone transformation. The 2025 join paper treats ask zeta functions and graphical-group class counting, including generic-row operations, but not irreducible-character degree multiplicities or full finite-field rank distributions. value.rationale: Rossmann's character-enumeration question is explicitly motivated by the difficulty of support-constrained rank loci. The result gives a closure operation on that problem: every known polynomial rank-enumeration family immediately generates infinitely many new graphs by repeated coning. Applying it to complete bipartite graphs yields a closed all-characteristic formula for the natural complete-tripartite family K_{1,a,b} and, by iteration, the complete multipartite family with arbitrarily many singleton parts. The contribution is structural rather than a one-off finite computation.
